Exactly one trunk variant. The type does not load without one, and two is an error.

#### `fallen_trunk.log_decoration_feature` {#fallen_trunk-log_decoration_feature}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · feature identifier · absent: nothing is run over the logs · edited on the connection, not in the form</p>

**A feature run once at every log of the fallen log itself.**

Placed at the log's own position, immediately after the log is written, and never at the stump. Unlike the delegation every Proxy feature does, this one is not subject to the internal-feature permission check -- a fallen trunk runs it whenever the reference resolves. An unresolved reference is not an error: nothing is run and the log is laid bare.

#### `poplar_trunk.log_decoration_feature` {#poplar_trunk-log_decoration_feature}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · feature identifier · absent: nothing is run over the column · edited on the connection, not in the form</p>

**A feature run once at every cell of the poplar's own column.**

Every cell the column walks, including a cell whose own log was refused by `may_replace` -- so the count of runs follows the sampled height, not the number of logs that actually went down. An unresolved reference is not an error: nothing is run.

:::: details `trunk` — 16 keys

#### `trunk` {#trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The plain trunk: one straight column of logs, and nothing else.**

The bare key is the SIMPLE shape, not a default that becomes something else once you fill it in. It takes five keys -- trunk_height and trunk_block are required, height_modifier, can_be_submerged and trunk_decoration are optional -- and has no trunk_width, no trunk_lean and no branches. It also hands its canopy an empty list of trunk positions, so pairing it with a canopy that scatters leaves over those positions grows a bare pole.

#### `trunk.trunk_height` {#trunk-trunk_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How many logs tall the column is, drawn once per tree.**

A range, so write a number for a fixed height or `{range_min, range_max}` for a varying one. A range object spelled `{min, max}` is not read: the engine reports the two members as missing and uses a height of 0, which loads and grows nothing.

#### `trunk.height_modifier` {#trunk-height_modifier}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {0, 0} -- adds nothing, and costs no draw</p>

**A second draw added to the trunk height.**

Drawn separately from trunk_height and added to it, so the two ranges compose. Leaving it out adds nothing and costs no draw at all, which keeps everything placed after this tree in the same spot.

#### `trunk.can_be_submerged` {#trunk-can_be_submerged}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no descent: the column starts at the origin</p>

**Lets the trunk start below the surface instead of at the origin.**

Before building, the column walks downward through blocks listed in may_grow_through and starts from where it stops. This is an option ON the plain trunk and never a choice of trunk shape -- the bare key is the plain trunk with or without it.

Also accepts a bare `true`, which means a maximum depth of 255, and a bare `false`, which means the same as leaving the key out.

#### `trunk.can_be_submerged.max_depth` {#trunk-can_be_submerged-max_depth}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The furthest down the trunk may start, in blocks.**

Required inside the object form. Writing the whole key as `true` instead means a maximum depth of 255, and writing `false`, or leaving it out, means no descent at all.

#### `trunk.trunk_block` {#trunk-trunk_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log the trunk column is built out of.**

Required on every trunk shape. Several shapes place sideways logs too -- branches, and a fallen log -- and those are this same block turned to lie along the direction they run in, so there is no second key for them.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration` {#trunk-trunk_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no decoration -- logs are placed bare</p>

**Blocks hung off the sides of the logs, such as vines.**

On this shape it is offered on all four sides of every log the column places. Each enabled side rolls decoration_chance independently, and only a side that wins its roll and finds a free cell gets anything. Up and down are never offered, on any trunk shape.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · chance · absent: 0, which decorates nothing at all</p>

**How often one side of one log gets decorated.**

Either a percent -- 100 always, 0 never -- or a {numerator, denominator} fraction. Mind the default: a trunk_decoration written without this key rolls 0 and therefore places nothing, so the decoration looks silently ignored rather than sparse.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance.numerator` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-numerator}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The top half of a fractional decoration chance.**

Used only when decoration_chance is written as an object. A numerator equal to the denominator always succeeds; anything else is compared against a draw below the denominator.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance.denominator` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-denominator}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The bottom half of a fractional decoration chance.**

A denominator of 0 never succeeds, and costs no draw. Otherwise the chance is numerator in denominator, drawn fresh for each side of each log.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList</p>

**A stack of decoration blocks placed outward from the log, in order.**

The entries share one running position: the first entry's run starts at the cell next to the log and each later entry continues from where the previous one stopped, rather than restarting. That is what lets a sequence spell "two of block A, then block B". Write this OR decoration_block, not both -- a sequence wins and the single block is ignored.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence.block` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block this run of the sequence places.**

Accepted as a bare name string, as `{name, states}`, or as `{tags: "<Molang query>"}`. It is turned to face the log before it is written, so a vine-like block attaches the right way.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence.count` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-count}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {1, 1} -- a single block, placed at the cell next to the log</p>

**How many blocks this entry of the sequence places.**

A range, so it can differ per log. The run stops early at the first cell that is not free, and the next entry carries on from wherever it stopped.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_block` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_block}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · block</p>

**One block hung on the log, the short form.**

Exactly the same as a decoration_blocks_sequence of one entry with a count of 1, and this is the spelling most trees use. Ignored when decoration_blocks_sequence is also present.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.num_steps` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-num_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer</p>

**Accepted here, but it changes nothing on a trunk decoration.**

The number of blocks placed comes from each sequence entry's own count, and nothing reads this key while placing them. It is accepted rather than refused so that a pack that already writes it still loads.

#### `trunk.trunk_decoration.step_direction` {#trunk-trunk_decoration-step_direction}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: down</p>

**Which way a run of decoration blocks stacks from the log.**

Only visible on a run longer than one block: the first block of every entry lands in the same cell whatever this says. Mind the default -- it is `down`, not outward.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `down` — Each run hangs downward from the log. The default, and what a vine-like decoration wants: the run grows toward the ground one cell at a time.
- `up` — Each run climbs upward from the log. The run grows toward the sky one cell at a time, alongside the trunk rather than away from it.
- `out` — Each run grows away from the log, horizontally. It follows the same direction that chose the cell -- so a run on the north side keeps going north.
- `away` — The same as `out`, spelled differently. Both spellings are accepted and behave identically; there is no reason to prefer one over the other.

:::: details `acacia_trunk` — 23 keys

#### `acacia_trunk` {#acacia_trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**A column that leans off to one side near the top, then branches.**

A different key set from the plain trunk: trunk_width, an object-shaped trunk_height and trunk_lean are all required, and there is no can_be_submerged. The lean begins a drawn number of blocks BELOW the top of the trunk, not above the ground.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_height` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The height of the column, as a base plus optional random steps.**

An object, not a range: `base` is the fixed part and `intervals` adds the variation. Writing a plain number here is refused, which is the quickest way to tell this shape apart from the plain trunk.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_height.base` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_height-base}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The fixed part of the trunk height, in blocks.**

Everything `intervals` draws is added on top of this, so it is the shortest the tree can be.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_height.intervals` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_height-intervals}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList · absent: no intervals -- the height is exactly `base`, with no draw at all</p>

**Extra random height added on top of `base`, one draw per entry.**

Each entry adds a draw between 0 and that entry's own value, so `[3, 3]` adds nought to four and `[5]` adds nought to four in one lumpier step. Leaving the list out makes the height exactly `base` every time, with no variation at all.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_height.min_height_for_canopy` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_height-min_height_for_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 3</p>

**How far up the trunk must reach before a canopy may sit on it.**

It gates where the canopy may ANCHOR, never where logs are placed: a trunk that never gets this high still builds its column, but hands the canopy nowhere to grow and comes out bare. It lives inside trunk_height rather than trunk_lean, which is easy to get wrong.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_width` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_width}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [1, −]</p>

**How many blocks across the trunk column is.**

The column is a square of this many logs on each side, so 2 is a four-log column. It also decides which logs count as being on an edge, and only edge logs can carry a decoration.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_lean` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_lean}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The sideways step the top of the trunk takes.**

Required. A single horizontal direction is picked at random, and from lean_height blocks below the top the column starts stepping that way once per block for lean_steps blocks.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_lean.allow_diagonal_growth` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_lean-allow_diagonal_growth}

<p class="fl-facts">required · boolean</p>

**Picks which of two completely different branch routines runs.**

Required, and getting it wrong does not shift the shape slightly, it swaps it: true grows at most ONE branch off a random side, false sweeps the trunk perimeter and can grow one per cell. The two even draw branch_length and branch_position in opposite orders, and only the true path decorates its branch logs.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_lean.lean_height` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_lean-lean_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far below the top of the trunk the lean starts.**

Counted DOWN from the top, not up from the ground: a draw of 1 leans over the last block, and a draw as large as the height leans from the very bottom.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_lean.lean_steps` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_lean-lean_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How many blocks the trunk steps sideways once it starts leaning.**

One step per block of height, all in the same direction, so this is also how far the top of the tree ends up from its base.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_lean.lean_length` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_lean-lean_length}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {0, 0} -- no sideways run past the top of the trunk</p>

**Extra logs laid sideways at the very top of the lean.**

It extends the column past trunk_height while the height stops rising, so it grows a horizontal run at the top rather than a taller tree. Left out it adds nothing and costs no draw.

#### `acacia_trunk.branches` {#acacia_trunk-branches}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no branch is grown -- but see the note: the branch pass still runs</p>

**The branch grown off the side of the trunk.**

Optional, but leaving it out is not the same as switching branches off: the branch pass runs on every acacia trunk and still spends its direction draw, it simply rolls a chance of 0 and places nothing. All three of branch_length, branch_position and branch_chance are required once the object is present.

#### `acacia_trunk.branches.branch_length` {#acacia_trunk-branches-branch_length}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far the branch reaches out from the trunk.**

Counted in steps, not in logs placed: a step into a blocked cell still moves the branch along and still uses up one of its length, it just leaves no log there.

#### `acacia_trunk.branches.branch_position` {#acacia_trunk-branches-branch_position}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far below the start of the lean the branch leaves the trunk.**

Subtracted from where the lean begins. A value that puts the branch above the top of the trunk grows no branch at all, and the draws are still spent.

#### `acacia_trunk.branches.branch_chance` {#acacia_trunk-branches-branch_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · chance</p>

**How often a branch is grown at all.**

Required inside `branches`. Either a percent or a {numerator, denominator} fraction. The random direction is drawn BEFORE this is rolled, and a branch pointing the same way the trunk leans is dropped, so even 100 does not mean every tree gets one.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance) — [`numerator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-numerator), [`denominator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-denominator).

#### `acacia_trunk.branches.branch_canopy` {#acacia_trunk-branches-branch_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · json · absent: no canopy is grown at the branch tips</p>

**A canopy grown at the tip of each branch this trunk makes.**

Separate from the tree's own canopy key and shaped independently of it -- the branch tips always ask for a canopy one block wide, whatever trunk_width says. Write exactly one canopy variant key inside it; none and two are both reported.

::: warning Free-text field
A whole canopy body: exactly one canopy variant key, from the same set the tree's own canopy offers, and every one of those variants is described elsewhere in this panel. What is missing here is the control, not the knowledge -- a choice of one nested inside another field is not something this editor can draw yet, so it is edited as JSON. Writing two canopy keys here, or none, is reported rather than ignored.
:::

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_block` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log the trunk column is built out of.**

Required on every trunk shape. Several shapes place sideways logs too -- branches, and a fallen log -- and those are this same block turned to lie along the direction they run in, so there is no second key for them.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_decoration` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no decoration -- logs are placed bare</p>

**Blocks hung off the sides of the logs, such as vines.**

On this shape it is offered on the outward sides of every edge log of the column, and on all four sides of each branch log. Each enabled side rolls decoration_chance independently, and only a side that wins its roll and finds a free cell gets anything. Up and down are never offered, on any trunk shape.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · chance · absent: 0, which decorates nothing at all</p>

**How often one side of one log gets decorated.**

Either a percent -- 100 always, 0 never -- or a {numerator, denominator} fraction. Mind the default: a trunk_decoration written without this key rolls 0 and therefore places nothing, so the decoration looks silently ignored rather than sparse.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance) — [`numerator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-numerator), [`denominator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-denominator).

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList</p>

**A stack of decoration blocks placed outward from the log, in order.**

The entries share one running position: the first entry's run starts at the cell next to the log and each later entry continues from where the previous one stopped, rather than restarting. That is what lets a sequence spell "two of block A, then block B". Write this OR decoration_block, not both -- a sequence wins and the single block is ignored.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence) — [`block`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-block), [`count`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-count).

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_block` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_block}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · block</p>

**One block hung on the log, the short form.**

Exactly the same as a decoration_blocks_sequence of one entry with a count of 1, and this is the spelling most trees use. Ignored when decoration_blocks_sequence is also present.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_decoration.num_steps` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_decoration-num_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer</p>

**Accepted here, but it changes nothing on a trunk decoration.**

The number of blocks placed comes from each sequence entry's own count, and nothing reads this key while placing them. It is accepted rather than refused so that a pack that already writes it still loads.

#### `acacia_trunk.trunk_decoration.step_direction` {#acacia_trunk-trunk_decoration-step_direction}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: down</p>

**Which way a run of decoration blocks stacks from the log.**

Only visible on a run longer than one block: the first block of every entry lands in the same cell whatever this says. Mind the default -- it is `down`, not outward.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `down` — Each run hangs downward from the log. The default, and what a vine-like decoration wants: the run grows toward the ground one cell at a time.
- `up` — Each run climbs upward from the log. The run grows toward the sky one cell at a time, alongside the trunk rather than away from it.
- `out` — Each run grows away from the log, horizontally. It follows the same direction that chose the cell -- so a run on the north side keeps going north.
- `away` — The same as `out`, spelled differently. Both spellings are accepted and behave identically; there is no reason to prefer one over the other.

:::: details `cherry_trunk` — 14 keys

#### `cherry_trunk` {#cherry_trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**A trunk that forks into one, two, or two branches plus a stem.**

The shape is drawn from tree_type_weights, and each resulting tip grows its own canopy. This is the one trunk with no canopy key of its own at tree level -- write the canopy inside branches.branch_canopy instead.

#### `cherry_trunk.trunk_height` {#cherry_trunk-trunk_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The height of the stem, as a base plus optional random steps.**

An object of `base` and `intervals`, like the acacia and mega trunks, not a range. The base must be at least 2, because a fork needs a stem under it to leave from.

#### `cherry_trunk.trunk_height.base` {#cherry_trunk-trunk_height-base}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [2, −]</p>

**The fixed part of the stem height, at least 2 blocks.**

Anything `intervals` draws is added on top. Below 2 there is no stem for the branches to fork from.

#### `cherry_trunk.trunk_height.intervals` {#cherry_trunk-trunk_height-intervals}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList · absent: no intervals -- the height is exactly `base`, with no draw at all</p>

**Extra random height added on top of `base`, one draw per entry.**

Each entry adds a draw between 0 and that entry's own value INCLUDED, one wider than the acacia and mega trunks get from the same list: with `base` 5 and `[2]` this trunk is 5 to 7 where theirs is 5 to 6. Leaving the list out makes the height exactly `base` every time.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches` {#cherry_trunk-branches}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The fork: how many branches, how long, and where they leave the stem.**

Required -- unlike the acacia and mega trunks, a cherry trunk without this object does not load. branch_horizontal_length, branch_start_offset_from_top and branch_end_offset_from_top are each required inside it.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches.tree_type_weights` {#cherry_trunk-branches-tree_type_weights}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: all three weights 0, which always grows the single-branch shape</p>

**The weighted choice between the three fork shapes.**

All three weights are required once the object is written, and they are relative rather than percentages. Leaving the whole object out leaves every weight at 0, which always produces the single-branch shape.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches.tree_type_weights.one_branch` {#cherry_trunk-branches-tree_type_weights-one_branch}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**Weight of the shape with a single branch off the stem.**

One tip, so one canopy. The stem stops where the branch leaves it.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches.tree_type_weights.two_branches` {#cherry_trunk-branches-tree_type_weights-two_branches}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**Weight of the shape with two branches on opposite sides.**

Two tips and two canopies. The second branch always leaves in the direction opposite the first.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches.tree_type_weights.two_branches_and_trunk` {#cherry_trunk-branches-tree_type_weights-two_branches_and_trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**Weight of the shape with two branches and a stem that keeps going.**

Three canopies: one at each branch tip and one on top of the stem, which runs the full height.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches.branch_horizontal_length` {#cherry_trunk-branches-branch_horizontal_length}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range · range [2, −]</p>

**How far out from the stem each branch reaches.**

Both ends of the range must be at least 2 -- a branch shorter than that has nowhere to put its bend, and the file is refused rather than silently straightened.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches.branch_start_offset_from_top` {#cherry_trunk-branches-branch_start_offset_from_top}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range · range [−, 0]</p>

**How far below the top of the stem a branch leaves it.**

Counted downward, so both ends of the range must be 0 or negative; -4 leaves the stem four blocks below its top. The two branches draw this separately and can start at different heights.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches.branch_end_offset_from_top` {#cherry_trunk-branches-branch_end_offset_from_top}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How high the branch tip finishes, relative to the top of the stem.**

Together with the start offset this is what makes a branch rise or fall along its length, and it is where the canopy for that branch is anchored.

#### `cherry_trunk.branches.branch_canopy` {#cherry_trunk-branches-branch_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · json · absent: no canopy is grown at the branch tips</p>

**A canopy grown at the tip of each branch this trunk makes.**

Separate from the tree's own canopy key and shaped independently of it -- the branch tips always ask for a canopy one block wide, whatever trunk_width says. Write exactly one canopy variant key inside it; none and two are both reported.

::: warning Free-text field
A whole canopy body: exactly one canopy variant key, from the same set the tree's own canopy offers, and every one of those variants is described elsewhere in this panel. What is missing here is the control, not the knowledge -- a choice of one nested inside another field is not something this editor can draw yet, so it is edited as JSON. Writing two canopy keys here, or none, is reported rather than ignored.
:::

#### `cherry_trunk.trunk_block` {#cherry_trunk-trunk_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log the trunk column is built out of.**

Required on every trunk shape. Several shapes place sideways logs too -- branches, and a fallen log -- and those are this same block turned to lie along the direction they run in, so there is no second key for them.

:::: details `fallen_trunk` — 11 keys

#### `fallen_trunk` {#fallen_trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**A log lying on the ground, with a short stump beside it.**

It is the one trunk shape that needs no canopy at all. The log drops to the ground first, then the whole run is checked before anything is written: if any cell is blocked, or three cells in a row have nothing under them, no log is placed -- though the stump is still built.

#### `fallen_trunk.log_length` {#fallen_trunk-log_length}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How long the fallen log is before modifiers.**

The log actually written is log_length plus height_modifier minus 2 blocks long, so a log_length of 5 lays 3 blocks unless height_modifier adds more.

#### `fallen_trunk.height_modifier` {#fallen_trunk-height_modifier}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {0, 0} -- the log is log_length minus 2 blocks long</p>

**A second draw added to the fallen log's length.**

Drawn separately and added to log_length. Left out it adds nothing and costs no draw.

#### `fallen_trunk.stump_height` {#fallen_trunk-stump_height}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {1, 1} -- a single stump block</p>

**How many blocks of upright stump stand next to the log.**

Mind the default: it is a single block, not none. The stump is also what decides success -- a fallen tree whose stump placed nothing counts as failed even when the log itself went down.

#### `fallen_trunk.trunk_block` {#fallen_trunk-trunk_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log the trunk column is built out of.**

Required on every trunk shape. Several shapes place sideways logs too -- branches, and a fallen log -- and those are this same block turned to lie along the direction they run in, so there is no second key for them.

#### `fallen_trunk.trunk_decoration` {#fallen_trunk-trunk_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no decoration -- logs are placed bare</p>

**Blocks hung off the sides of the logs, such as vines.**

On this shape it is offered on all four sides of each block of the upright stump, and not on the fallen log. Each enabled side rolls decoration_chance independently, and only a side that wins its roll and finds a free cell gets anything. Up and down are never offered, on any trunk shape.

#### `fallen_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance` {#fallen_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · chance · absent: 0, which decorates nothing at all</p>

**How often one side of one log gets decorated.**

Either a percent -- 100 always, 0 never -- or a {numerator, denominator} fraction. Mind the default: a trunk_decoration written without this key rolls 0 and therefore places nothing, so the decoration looks silently ignored rather than sparse.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance) — [`numerator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-numerator), [`denominator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-denominator).

#### `fallen_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence` {#fallen_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList</p>

**A stack of decoration blocks placed outward from the log, in order.**

The entries share one running position: the first entry's run starts at the cell next to the log and each later entry continues from where the previous one stopped, rather than restarting. That is what lets a sequence spell "two of block A, then block B". Write this OR decoration_block, not both -- a sequence wins and the single block is ignored.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence) — [`block`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-block), [`count`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-count).

#### `fallen_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_block` {#fallen_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_block}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · block</p>

**One block hung on the log, the short form.**

Exactly the same as a decoration_blocks_sequence of one entry with a count of 1, and this is the spelling most trees use. Ignored when decoration_blocks_sequence is also present.

#### `fallen_trunk.trunk_decoration.num_steps` {#fallen_trunk-trunk_decoration-num_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer</p>

**Accepted here, but it changes nothing on a trunk decoration.**

The number of blocks placed comes from each sequence entry's own count, and nothing reads this key while placing them. It is accepted rather than refused so that a pack that already writes it still loads.

#### `fallen_trunk.trunk_decoration.step_direction` {#fallen_trunk-trunk_decoration-step_direction}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: down</p>

**Which way a run of decoration blocks stacks from the log.**

Only visible on a run longer than one block: the first block of every entry lands in the same cell whatever this says. Mind the default -- it is `down`, not outward.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `down` — Each run hangs downward from the log. The default, and what a vine-like decoration wants: the run grows toward the ground one cell at a time.
- `up` — Each run climbs upward from the log. The run grows toward the sky one cell at a time, alongside the trunk rather than away from it.
- `out` — Each run grows away from the log, horizontally. It follows the same direction that chose the cell -- so a run on the north side keeps going north.
- `away` — The same as `out`, spelled differently. Both spellings are accepted and behave identically; there is no reason to prefer one over the other.

::::

:::: details `fancy_trunk` — 13 keys

#### `fancy_trunk` {#fancy_trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The big branching oak: scattered foliage clusters with limbs drawn out to them.**

Not a leaning trunk with a crown on top. It picks foliage positions around the tree, grows a canopy at each, and draws a limb from the trunk out to every one high enough to qualify. All of trunk_height, trunk_width, width_scale, foliage_altitude_factor, branches and trunk_block are required.

#### `fancy_trunk.trunk_height` {#fancy_trunk-trunk_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The height of the tree, as a base, a variance and a trunk scale.**

An object with all three members required. Note that the tree height and the COLUMN height are different numbers here -- see `scale`.

#### `fancy_trunk.trunk_height.base` {#fancy_trunk-trunk_height-base}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The fixed part of the overall tree height.**

Also the floor under which a blocked trunk is not shortened: a trunk blocked above this height simply comes out shorter, and one blocked below it fails to grow at all.

#### `fancy_trunk.trunk_height.variance` {#fancy_trunk-trunk_height-variance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [1, −]</p>

**How much the tree height varies from tree to tree.**

Must be at least 1. One draw between 0 and this value is added to `base` for each tree.

#### `fancy_trunk.trunk_height.scale` {#fancy_trunk-trunk_height-scale}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**The fraction of the tree height the log column actually reaches.**

Below 1 the column stops short of the top of the tree, which is normal here and not a defect: foliage routinely sits above the last log. A short height draw can leave the foliage overlapping the trunk, which is also what the game does.

#### `fancy_trunk.trunk_width` {#fancy_trunk-trunk_width}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [1, −]</p>

**How many blocks across the log column is.**

A square of this many logs per side, the same as on the acacia and mega trunks.

#### `fancy_trunk.width_scale` {#fancy_trunk-width_scale}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**How far out from the trunk the foliage clusters sit.**

It scales the radius of the ring of foliage positions, so a larger value spreads the crown wider and makes the limbs reaching out to it longer.

#### `fancy_trunk.foliage_altitude_factor` {#fancy_trunk-foliage_altitude_factor}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**How the foliage spread changes with height up the tree.**

The crown is shaped along a curved profile rather than a cylinder, and this is what bends it: it decides how wide the ring of foliage positions is at each height.

#### `fancy_trunk.branches` {#fancy_trunk-branches}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The limbs drawn from the trunk out to the foliage clusters.**

Required on this shape, unlike the acacia and mega trunks where the branches object is optional. All three of slope, density and min_altitude_factor are required inside it.

#### `fancy_trunk.branches.slope` {#fancy_trunk-branches-slope}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**How steeply a limb climbs as it reaches outward.**

It sets where on the trunk a limb starts, so a steeper slope attaches it lower down.

#### `fancy_trunk.branches.density` {#fancy_trunk-branches-density}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**How many foliage clusters, and so how many limbs, the tree gets.**

Scaled by the height of the tree, so a taller tree with the same density carries more clusters.

#### `fancy_trunk.branches.min_altitude_factor` {#fancy_trunk-branches-min_altitude_factor}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**How high up a cluster must be before a limb is drawn to it.**

Clusters below it still grow their canopy -- they simply float, with no limb connecting them to the trunk. Limbs are also written without checking may_replace, so they overwrite whatever they cross.

#### `fancy_trunk.trunk_block` {#fancy_trunk-trunk_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log the trunk column is built out of.**

Required on every trunk shape. Several shapes place sideways logs too -- branches, and a fallen log -- and those are this same block turned to lie along the direction they run in, so there is no second key for them.

::::

:::: details `mangrove_trunk` — 17 keys

#### `mangrove_trunk` {#mangrove_trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The mangrove trunk: a thin column that sprouts short angled branches.**

The shape that pairs with the top-level mangrove_roots key, though the roots run for every trunk shape. Its trunk_height is an object of base plus two random terms, which is unlike every other trunk shape.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_width` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_width}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer</p>

**Accepted here, but it changes nothing on this shape.**

The mangrove column is always one block across whatever this says. It is accepted rather than refused so a pack that already writes it still loads.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_height` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The height, as a fixed base plus two independent random terms.**

An object, and all three members are required. Two separate draws are added to `base`, which piles the result toward the middle instead of spreading it evenly like a range would.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_height.base` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_height-base}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The fixed part of the mangrove trunk height.**

Both random terms are added on top of it, so it is the shortest the column can be.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_height.height_rand_a` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_height-height_rand_a}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**The first random term added to the mangrove height.**

One draw from 0 up to and including this value. A 0 here contributes nothing.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_height.height_rand_b` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_height-height_rand_b}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**The second random term added to the mangrove height.**

Drawn separately from the first and added as well, so the two together bunch the height around the middle of their combined span rather than spreading it evenly.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_block` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log the trunk column is built out of.**

Required on every trunk shape. Several shapes place sideways logs too -- branches, and a fallen log -- and those are this same block turned to lie along the direction they run in, so there is no second key for them.

#### `mangrove_trunk.branches` {#mangrove_trunk-branches}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: branch_length and branch_steps both {0, 0} -- see the note, the branch pass still runs</p>

**The short angled branches that come off the mangrove column.**

Optional, and leaving it out is not the same as switching branches off: every non-final log flips a coin either way, and on a win a branch is grown using lengths of 0, which places nothing. Writing the object simply gives those draws something to work with.

#### `mangrove_trunk.branches.branch_length` {#mangrove_trunk-branches-branch_length}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {0, 0}</p>

**How far a mangrove branch reaches out.**

Drawn TWICE per branch, and both draws are used: the difference between them decides where along the branch the logs actually start, so a wide range makes a ragged tree rather than just a longer branch.

#### `mangrove_trunk.branches.branch_steps` {#mangrove_trunk-branches-branch_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {0, 0}</p>

**How many times a mangrove branch steps upward as it goes out.**

Drawn once per branch. It is what tilts the branch up rather than leaving it flat.

#### `mangrove_trunk.branches.branch_chance` {#mangrove_trunk-branches-branch_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · chance</p>

**Accepted here, but it changes nothing on this shape.**

Whether a mangrove branch is grown is decided by a plain coin flip that this key does not feed. A malformed value is still reported, so it has to be written correctly even though nothing reads it.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance) — [`numerator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-numerator), [`denominator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-denominator).

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_decoration` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no decoration -- logs are placed bare</p>

**Blocks hung off the sides of the logs, such as vines.**

On this shape it is offered on all four sides of every log, the topmost one included, and of every branch log. Each enabled side rolls decoration_chance independently, and only a side that wins its roll and finds a free cell gets anything. Up and down are never offered, on any trunk shape.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · chance · absent: 0, which decorates nothing at all</p>

**How often one side of one log gets decorated.**

Either a percent -- 100 always, 0 never -- or a {numerator, denominator} fraction. Mind the default: a trunk_decoration written without this key rolls 0 and therefore places nothing, so the decoration looks silently ignored rather than sparse.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance) — [`numerator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-numerator), [`denominator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-denominator).

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList</p>

**A stack of decoration blocks placed outward from the log, in order.**

The entries share one running position: the first entry's run starts at the cell next to the log and each later entry continues from where the previous one stopped, rather than restarting. That is what lets a sequence spell "two of block A, then block B". Write this OR decoration_block, not both -- a sequence wins and the single block is ignored.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence) — [`block`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-block), [`count`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-count).

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_block` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_block}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · block</p>

**One block hung on the log, the short form.**

Exactly the same as a decoration_blocks_sequence of one entry with a count of 1, and this is the spelling most trees use. Ignored when decoration_blocks_sequence is also present.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_decoration.num_steps` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_decoration-num_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer</p>

**Accepted here, but it changes nothing on a trunk decoration.**

The number of blocks placed comes from each sequence entry's own count, and nothing reads this key while placing them. It is accepted rather than refused so that a pack that already writes it still loads.

#### `mangrove_trunk.trunk_decoration.step_direction` {#mangrove_trunk-trunk_decoration-step_direction}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: down</p>

**Which way a run of decoration blocks stacks from the log.**

Only visible on a run longer than one block: the first block of every entry lands in the same cell whatever this says. Mind the default -- it is `down`, not outward.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `down` — Each run hangs downward from the log. The default, and what a vine-like decoration wants: the run grows toward the ground one cell at a time.
- `up` — Each run climbs upward from the log. The run grows toward the sky one cell at a time, alongside the trunk rather than away from it.
- `out` — Each run grows away from the log, horizontally. It follows the same direction that chose the cell -- so a run on the north side keeps going north.
- `away` — The same as `out`, spelled differently. Both spellings are accepted and behave identically; there is no reason to prefer one over the other.

::::

:::: details `mega_trunk` — 20 keys

#### `mega_trunk` {#mega_trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The wide trunk of a giant tree, with long sweeping branches.**

trunk_width is required and is usually 2 or more, which is what makes it "mega". It is the only trunk shape that builds the tree's top-level base_cluster -- written next to any other shape, that key is read and then never used.

#### `mega_trunk.trunk_height` {#mega_trunk-trunk_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The height of the column, as a base plus optional random steps.**

An object of `base` and `intervals`, the same shape the acacia and cherry trunks use, not a range.

#### `mega_trunk.trunk_height.base` {#mega_trunk-trunk_height-base}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The fixed part of the mega trunk height.**

Everything `intervals` draws is added on top of this. Giant trees need a tall preview volume to fit.

#### `mega_trunk.trunk_height.intervals` {#mega_trunk-trunk_height-intervals}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList · absent: no intervals -- the height is exactly `base`, with no draw at all</p>

**Extra random height added on top of `base`, one draw per entry.**

Each entry adds a draw between 0 and that entry's own value, so `[3, 3]` adds nought to four and `[5]` adds nought to four in one lumpier step. Leaving the list out makes the height exactly `base` every time, with no variation at all.

#### `mega_trunk.trunk_width` {#mega_trunk-trunk_width}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [1, −]</p>

**How many blocks across the wide column is.**

A square of this many logs per side. It also decides which logs are on an edge, and only edge logs carry a decoration -- and the topmost layer never does, whatever its width.

#### `mega_trunk.trunk_block` {#mega_trunk-trunk_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log the trunk column is built out of.**

Required on every trunk shape. Several shapes place sideways logs too -- branches, and a fallen log -- and those are this same block turned to lie along the direction they run in, so there is no second key for them.

#### `mega_trunk.branches` {#mega_trunk-branches}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no branches at all -- the trunk is a bare column</p>

**The long branches that sweep out from the column.**

Optional, and here absence really does mean no branches at all. The branches are built BEFORE the column, so a log of the trunk placed afterwards can overwrite a branch log that crossed it. branch_length, branch_slope, branch_interval and branch_altitude_factor are all required once the object is present.

#### `mega_trunk.branches.branch_length` {#mega_trunk-branches-branch_length}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**How many logs long each branch is.**

A plain whole number, not a range, so every branch on the tree is the same length. The logs are written without checking may_replace, so a branch goes straight through whatever is there.

#### `mega_trunk.branches.branch_slope` {#mega_trunk-branches-branch_slope}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**How steeply each branch climbs as it reaches out.**

Applied per log, so it also decides how far below the branch's anchor height the branch starts.

#### `mega_trunk.branches.branch_interval` {#mega_trunk-branches-branch_interval}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**The vertical gap between one branch and the next.**

Drawn fresh for each gap, so the branches are unevenly spaced up the trunk. Branches keep being added downward until the next gap would take them below where branches are allowed.

#### `mega_trunk.branches.branch_altitude_factor` {#mega_trunk-branches-branch_altitude_factor}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**The band of the trunk, top and bottom, that carries branches.**

Both members are fractions of the tree height: `max` is where the topmost branch may sit and `min` is the lowest. This object is the one place in a trunk body that really is spelled `min` and `max` -- everywhere else those two names are the wrong spelling of a range.

A plain two-member object, NOT a range: this one really is spelled `min` and `max`.

#### `mega_trunk.branches.branch_altitude_factor.min` {#mega_trunk-branches-branch_altitude_factor-min}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**The lowest point on the trunk that may carry a branch.**

A fraction of the tree height, so 0.4 means branches stop about two fifths of the way up.

#### `mega_trunk.branches.branch_altitude_factor.max` {#mega_trunk-branches-branch_altitude_factor-max}

<p class="fl-facts">required · number</p>

**The highest point on the trunk that may carry a branch.**

A fraction of the tree height, and where the first branch is placed before the gaps walk downward.

#### `mega_trunk.branches.branch_canopy` {#mega_trunk-branches-branch_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · json · absent: no canopy is grown at the branch tips</p>

**A canopy grown at the tip of each branch this trunk makes.**

Separate from the tree's own canopy key and shaped independently of it -- the branch tips always ask for a canopy one block wide, whatever trunk_width says. Write exactly one canopy variant key inside it; none and two are both reported.

::: warning Free-text field
A whole canopy body: exactly one canopy variant key, from the same set the tree's own canopy offers, and every one of those variants is described elsewhere in this panel. What is missing here is the control, not the knowledge -- a choice of one nested inside another field is not something this editor can draw yet, so it is edited as JSON. Writing two canopy keys here, or none, is reported rather than ignored.
:::

#### `mega_trunk.trunk_decoration` {#mega_trunk-trunk_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no decoration -- logs are placed bare</p>

**Blocks hung off the sides of the logs, such as vines.**

On this shape it is offered on the outward sides of every edge log below the top layer -- the topmost layer of logs is never decorated. Each enabled side rolls decoration_chance independently, and only a side that wins its roll and finds a free cell gets anything. Up and down are never offered, on any trunk shape.

<p class="fl-facts">optional · block</p>

**One block hung on the log, the short form.**

Exactly the same as a decoration_blocks_sequence of one entry with a count of 1, and this is the spelling most trees use. Ignored when decoration_blocks_sequence is also present.

#### `mega_trunk.trunk_decoration.num_steps` {#mega_trunk-trunk_decoration-num_steps}

#### `mega_trunk.trunk_decoration.step_direction` {#mega_trunk-trunk_decoration-step_direction}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: down</p>

**Which way a run of decoration blocks stacks from the log.**

- `out` — Each run grows away from the log, horizontally. It follows the same direction that chose the cell -- so a run on the north side keeps going north.
