:::: details `poplar_trunk` — 11 keys

#### `poplar_trunk` {#poplar_trunk}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · 1.26.50.24</p>

**A tall narrow column with a small ring of branches near the top.**

Added in game version 1.26.50. The branches are short stubs that support the crown rather than limbs of their own, and the canopy is anchored just above them rather than on top of the column.

#### `poplar_trunk.trunk_height` {#poplar_trunk-trunk_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How many logs tall the poplar column is.**

A range, like the plain trunk and unlike the acacia, mega, cherry, fancy and mangrove trunks, all of which want an object here. Required, even though the shape has a height of its own it would otherwise fall back on.

#### `poplar_trunk.remaining_trunk_height_above_branches` {#poplar_trunk-remaining_trunk_height_above_branches}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {4, 4} -- four blocks of bare trunk above the branch ring, with no draw</p>

**How much bare trunk is left standing above the branch ring.**

Measured down from the top, so a larger value pushes the branches and the canopy lower without making the tree shorter. The default of four blocks is a fixed number and costs no draw.

#### `poplar_trunk.amount_of_foliage_support_branches` {#poplar_trunk-amount_of_foliage_support_branches}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: {1, 4} -- one to four branches</p>

**How many short branches ring the trunk under the crown.**

The directions are shuffled first, so a count of 2 picks two different sides at random. There are only four sides, so anything above 4 behaves exactly like 4.

#### `poplar_trunk.trunk_block` {#poplar_trunk-trunk_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log the trunk column is built out of.**

Required on every trunk shape. Several shapes place sideways logs too -- branches, and a fallen log -- and those are this same block turned to lie along the direction they run in, so there is no second key for them.

#### `poplar_trunk.trunk_decoration` {#poplar_trunk-trunk_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no decoration -- logs are placed bare</p>

**Blocks hung off the sides of the logs, such as vines.**

On this shape it is offered on all four sides of every log of the column and of every branch stub. Each enabled side rolls decoration_chance independently, and only a side that wins its roll and finds a free cell gets anything. Up and down are never offered, on any trunk shape.

#### `poplar_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance` {#poplar_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · chance · absent: 0, which decorates nothing at all</p>

**How often one side of one log gets decorated.**

Either a percent -- 100 always, 0 never -- or a {numerator, denominator} fraction. Mind the default: a trunk_decoration written without this key rolls 0 and therefore places nothing, so the decoration looks silently ignored rather than sparse.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_chance`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance) — [`numerator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-numerator), [`denominator`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_chance-denominator).

#### `poplar_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence` {#poplar_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList</p>

**A stack of decoration blocks placed outward from the log, in order.**

The entries share one running position: the first entry's run starts at the cell next to the log and each later entry continues from where the previous one stopped, rather than restarting. That is what lets a sequence spell "two of block A, then block B". Write this OR decoration_block, not both -- a sequence wins and the single block is ignored.

Sub-keys: the same as [`trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence) — [`block`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-block), [`count`](#trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-count).

#### `poplar_trunk.trunk_decoration.decoration_block` {#poplar_trunk-trunk_decoration-decoration_block}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · block</p>

**One block hung on the log, the short form.**

Exactly the same as a decoration_blocks_sequence of one entry with a count of 1, and this is the spelling most trees use. Ignored when decoration_blocks_sequence is also present.

#### `poplar_trunk.trunk_decoration.num_steps` {#poplar_trunk-trunk_decoration-num_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer</p>

**Accepted here, but it changes nothing on a trunk decoration.**

The number of blocks placed comes from each sequence entry's own count, and nothing reads this key while placing them. It is accepted rather than refused so that a pack that already writes it still loads.

#### `poplar_trunk.trunk_decoration.step_direction` {#poplar_trunk-trunk_decoration-step_direction}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: down</p>

**Which way a run of decoration blocks stacks from the log.**

Only visible on a run longer than one block: the first block of every entry lands in the same cell whatever this says. Mind the default -- it is `down`, not outward.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `down` — Each run hangs downward from the log. The default, and what a vine-like decoration wants: the run grows toward the ground one cell at a time.
- `up` — Each run climbs upward from the log. The run grows toward the sky one cell at a time, alongside the trunk rather than away from it.
- `out` — Each run grows away from the log, horizontally. It follows the same direction that chose the cell -- so a run on the north side keeps going north.
- `away` — The same as `out`, spelled differently. Both spellings are accepted and behave identically; there is no reason to prefer one over the other.

::::

:::: details `canopy` — 15 keys

#### `canopy` {#canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The generic canopy: a stack of filled squares over the trunk, widest at the bottom.**

The bare word is a real shape with its own key set, not a default that turns into one of the others. Each layer's half-width is min_width plus the drop from the top layer's slope to this one's, so with the default 1-to-1 slope and canopy_offset {min: -3, max: 0} the radii run 3, 2, 1, 0 from the bottom up -- the familiar oak crown.

#### `canopy.leaf_block` {#canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block every layer of the crown is built from.**

One block for the whole shape; this canopy has no second block and no weighting.

#### `canopy.canopy_offset` {#canopy-canopy_offset}

<p class="fl-facts">required · group</p>

**Which heights the layers occupy, measured from the top of the trunk.**

Mind the spelling: this is a plain object with members named min and max, NOT a range, so range_min and range_max do not work here and neither does the two-element array form. A negative min puts layers BELOW the point the trunk handed over.

#### `canopy.canopy_offset.min` {#canopy-canopy_offset-min}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The lowest layer, as an offset from the trunk top.**

Usually negative, because the crown normally starts below the trunk top and builds upward.

#### `canopy.canopy_offset.max` {#canopy-canopy_offset-max}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The highest layer, as an offset from the trunk top.**

Also the layer the whole taper is measured from: every other layer's width is worked out as its distance below this one, so moving max changes the width of every layer at once, not just the top.

#### `canopy.min_width` {#canopy-min_width}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 0</p>

**A half-width added to every layer, including the topmost.**

It widens the crown uniformly rather than changing its taper; canopy_slope is what changes the taper.

#### `canopy.canopy_slope` {#canopy-canopy_slope}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: a 1-to-1 slope -- one step of radius per layer</p>

**How fast the layers narrow going up, as a rise over a run.**

A run of 2 makes the crown lose half a step of width per layer, so it tapers half as fast and ends up taller for the same width. A run of zero is refused rather than divided by.

#### `canopy.canopy_slope.rise` {#canopy-canopy_slope-rise}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 1</p>

**The numerator of the taper: how much width is lost per run of layers.**

Raising it narrows the crown faster and leaves a smaller top.

#### `canopy.canopy_slope.run` {#canopy-canopy_slope-run}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 1</p>

**The denominator of the taper: how many layers one step of width is spread over.**

Raising it makes a taller, more column-like crown. Zero is refused.

#### `canopy.variation_chance` {#canopy-variation_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · json · absent: no corner is ever removed, and no random number is drawn for one</p>

**Chance to leave out each of the four corners of a layer, which is what rounds the square off.**

Four cells per layer -- where the horizontal and vertical distances from the centre both equal that layer's half-width -- are each rolled once. This is the only part of this canopy that draws random numbers at all. There is no guard for a one-cell layer: on a layer of half-width 0 that single centre cell IS all four corners, so a chance that always succeeds deletes the layer outright -- which is how a crown gets capped flat instead of ending in one leaf poking out of the top.

::: warning Free-text field
This key accepts three spellings and a single control cannot offer all three: a percent number, a {numerator, denominator} object, or an array of either with exactly one entry per canopy layer, ordered from canopy_offset.min upward. An array of the wrong length is refused. Write it as JSON.
:::

#### `canopy.canopy_decoration` {#canopy-canopy_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: nothing hangs off the canopy, and no random number is drawn for it</p>

**Hangs a block off the sides of the crown -- vines, typically.**

Each leaf the canopy places rolls once per horizontal neighbour; a success on a neighbour that is air writes a run of cells straight down from it, stopping at the first cell that is not air. Note that this object is NOT the same shape as the object of the same name on mangrove_canopy.

#### `canopy.canopy_decoration.decoration_block` {#canopy-canopy_decoration-decoration_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block written down the side of the crown.**

The whole run is this one block; there is no sequence form here.

#### `canopy.canopy_decoration.decoration_chance` {#canopy-canopy_decoration-decoration_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · chance</p>

**Chance that any one horizontal neighbour of a leaf starts a run.**

Rolled per leaf per neighbour, so a dense crown spends a great many rolls.

#### `canopy.canopy_decoration.num_steps` {#canopy-canopy_decoration-num_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How many cells long a run is, drawn per run.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. The run stops early at the first cell that is not air, so a long range does not guarantee a long strand.

#### `canopy.canopy_decoration.step_direction` {#canopy-canopy_decoration-step_direction}

<p class="fl-facts">required · enum</p>

**Which way the run grows. Only downward is accepted here.**

That is the direction vanilla's own definitions use and the only one whose behaviour has been established for this object, so any other spelling is refused rather than guessed at.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `down` — Grows the run straight down from the leaf it started at. The only value accepted for this object, and the one vanilla's own hanging vines use.

::::

:::: details `acacia_canopy` — 4 keys

#### `acacia_canopy` {#acacia_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The flat, spreading acacia crown: one wide octagonal ring with a smaller layer on top.**

Entirely fixed -- this shape draws no random numbers at all, so two acacias with the same settings get identical crowns.

#### `acacia_canopy.leaf_block` {#acacia_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block both layers of the crown are built from.**

One block for the whole crown -- this shape takes no second block and no weighted list, so the two layers always match.

#### `acacia_canopy.canopy_size` {#acacia_canopy-canopy_size}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The half-width of the lower ring.**

The lower layer is a square of this half-width minus its four exact corners. That corner cut has no guard for a size of 0: at 0 the single centre cell is itself a corner, so the lower layer comes out completely empty and only the upper layer is placed.

#### `acacia_canopy.simplify_canopy` {#acacia_canopy-simplify_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · boolean · absent: false</p>

**Replaces the upper layer's four protruding arms with a plain square.**

With it off, the upper layer is a narrower square with four single cells poking out along the axes. With it on, it is one filled square and nothing sticks out -- a cleaner, slightly smaller silhouette.

::::

:::: details `cherry_canopy` — 9 keys

#### `cherry_canopy` {#cherry_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The cherry crown: a rounded block of leaves with a fringe hanging below it.**

Built as a stack of square layers that widen toward the bottom, then two more layers below the anchor that also trail leaves downward. The cherry trunk grows one of these at each branch tip rather than one for the whole tree.

#### `cherry_canopy.leaf_block` {#cherry_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block the crown and its hanging fringe are built from.**

The fringe is the same block as the body; there is no separate hanging block on this shape.

#### `cherry_canopy.height` {#cherry_canopy-height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range · range [4, −]</p>

**How tall the crown is, drawn per crown. At least 4.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. The bottom four layers are fixed in shape and the remainder stack above them at full width, so raising this makes the crown taller without making it wider. Values below 4 leave the shape with no layers to build and are refused.

#### `cherry_canopy.radius` {#cherry_canopy-radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range · range [3, −]</p>

**How wide the crown is, drawn per crown. At least 3.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. The widest layers sit at this half-width; the top two step in by one and two cells. Values below 3 make the topmost layer inside-out and are refused.

#### `cherry_canopy.trunk_width` {#cherry_canopy-trunk_width}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 1 · range [1, 1]</p>

**The trunk footprint the crown is built around. Must be 1.**

Every trunk that can carry this crown hands it a one-block footprint, so any other value is refused rather than silently building a crown around a trunk that is not there.

#### `cherry_canopy.wide_bottom_layer_hole_chance` {#cherry_canopy-wide_bottom_layer_hole_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · chance</p>

**Chance to punch a hole in the outer edge of the widest bottom layer.**

Rolled per edge cell of that one layer. It is what stops the underside reading as a solid slab.

#### `cherry_canopy.corner_hole_chance` {#cherry_canopy-corner_hole_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · chance</p>

**Chance to leave out a corner cell of a layer.**

Which cells count as corners changes with the layer's width: a narrow layer rolls its four square corners, a wide one has its corners cut outright and instead rolls a ring just inside the edge.

#### `cherry_canopy.hanging_leaves_chance` {#cherry_canopy-hanging_leaves_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · chance</p>

**Chance to trail a leaf one cell below the crown's bottom edge.**

Rolled along the four straight edges of the two lowest layers -- the fringe that gives a cherry its drooping look.

#### `cherry_canopy.hanging_leaves_extension_chance` {#cherry_canopy-hanging_leaves_extension_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · chance</p>

**Chance to extend a trailing leaf by a second cell.**

Rolled only where the first leaf was actually placed, so this is a chance on a chance and a small value thins the fringe quickly.

::::

:::: details `fancy_canopy` — 4 keys

#### `fancy_canopy` {#fancy_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**A stack of round discs, full width in the middle and pulled in at the top and bottom.**

Each layer is a disc rather than a square, which is what makes this the roundest of the twelve. It draws no random numbers, so its shape is entirely fixed by its two numbers.

#### `fancy_canopy.leaf_block` {#fancy_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block every disc is built from.**

One block for the whole crown -- this shape takes no second block and no weighted list, so the discs come out a single solid colour.

#### `fancy_canopy.height` {#fancy_canopy-height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**How many discs are stacked.**

A height of 0 is legal and places nothing at all. A height of 1 gives a single pulled-in disc, since that one layer is both the top cap and the bottom.

#### `fancy_canopy.radius` {#fancy_canopy-radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · absent: the game treats this key as optional, but what it falls back to has not been established, so a value is asked for here rather than guessed · range [1, −]</p>

**The half-width of the middle discs.**

The top and bottom discs are one cell narrower than this. A radius below 1 would make those caps inside-out, so it is refused.

::::

:::: details `mangrove_canopy` — 15 keys

#### `mangrove_canopy` {#mangrove_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**A scattered crown of leaves with blocks hanging beneath it.**

Unlike the layered shapes, this scatters individual leaves around EVERY log the trunk placed, not just the top one. Pair it with a trunk that collects its logs -- with the plain trunk or the cherry trunk it is handed an empty list, places nothing and draws nothing, leaving a bare pole.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_height` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far up and down a scattered leaf may land, drawn once for the whole crown.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. One value is drawn per tree and then reused for every attempt.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_radius` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far sideways a scattered leaf may land, drawn once for the whole crown.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. Like the height, drawn once and shared by every attempt.

#### `mangrove_canopy.leaf_placement_attempts` {#mangrove_canopy-leaf_placement_attempts}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**How many leaves are attempted around each trunk log.**

Multiplied by the number of logs the trunk collected, so this number and the trunk height together decide how dense the crown is. An attempt that lands somewhere it may not build is simply lost.

#### `mangrove_canopy.leaf_blocks` {#mangrove_canopy-leaf_blocks}

<p class="fl-facts">required · weightedBlockList</p>

**The blocks the scattered leaves are picked from, with weights.**

Write each entry as a two-element pair: the block first, then its weight. The list may not be empty. One pick is made per leaf, so the weights decide the mix within a single crown rather than between trees.

#### `mangrove_canopy.hanging_block` {#mangrove_canopy-hanging_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block hung beneath the crown -- propagules, in vanilla.**

Placed in a separate pass after every leaf is down, so it hangs from the finished shape rather than from a partial one.

#### `mangrove_canopy.hanging_block_placement_chance` {#mangrove_canopy-hanging_block_placement_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · chance</p>

**Chance that any one candidate position below the crown gets a hanging block.**

This is the only gate on that pass: at zero the crown is leaves alone, and the hanging block never appears.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_decoration` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: nothing is attached to the scattered leaves, and no random number is drawn for it</p>

**Attaches a block to the sides of the hanging positions.**

Runs before the hanging blocks themselves, once per candidate, with all four horizontal sides eligible. Note that this object is a DIFFERENT shape from the object of the same name on the generic canopy: it takes a block sequence and a four-way step direction, where that one takes a single block and only accepts downward.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_decoration.decoration_block` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_decoration-decoration_block}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · block · absent: no block, unless decoration_blocks_sequence supplies one</p>

**A single block to attach.**

An alternative to decoration_blocks_sequence, not an addition to it -- when the sequence is present this is not read.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · groupList · absent: the single decoration_block is used instead</p>

**An ordered list of block runs to attach, one after another from the same starting cell.**

Each run stops early the moment its next cell is not air, so a later run can be cut short by what an earlier one built.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence.block` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block this run is made of.**

Required on every entry; an entry without one has nothing to place.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_decoration.decoration_blocks_sequence.count` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_decoration-decoration_blocks_sequence-count}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · range · absent: one block</p>

**How many cells long this run is, drawn per run.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. Leaving it out gives a run of exactly one block.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_decoration.decoration_chance` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_decoration-decoration_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">required · chance</p>

**Chance that any one eligible side is decorated.**

Rolled per side per candidate position. At zero nothing is attached and the whole object has no effect.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_decoration.num_steps` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_decoration-num_steps}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: nothing -- the value is accepted and never read</p>

**Accepted and then ignored -- this key has no effect.**

The game reads the key and stores it, and the code that places the decoration never looks at it. It is listed so that finding it in an existing file is not mistaken for a setting that stopped working. Use the count on each sequence entry to control run length instead.

#### `mangrove_canopy.canopy_decoration.step_direction` {#mangrove_canopy-canopy_decoration-step_direction}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · enum · absent: down</p>

**Which way a run of more than one block grows.**

Only runs longer than one cell can tell the difference, so on a single-block decoration this changes nothing.

Values, in the order the engine lists them:

- `down` — Grows each run downward from its starting cell. The default, and what a hanging decoration wants.
- `up` — Grows each run upward from its starting cell. The mirror of down; a run still stops at the first cell that is not air.
- `out` — Grows each run outward, away from the block it is attached to. The run reaches sideways into open space rather than along the crown.
- `away` — The same as out -- a second spelling of the outward direction. Written either way it behaves identically, so pick whichever reads better in your file.

::::

:::: details `mega_canopy` — 6 keys

#### `mega_canopy` {#mega_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**A broad cone for a wide trunk, flaring outward toward the bottom.**

Each layer is one cell wider than the one above it, so the crown reads as a solid downward-flaring cone rather than a ball.

#### `mega_canopy.leaf_block` {#mega_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block every layer of the cone is built from.**

One block for the whole cone. Unlike the two scattering canopies there is no weighted list here, so a mega crown cannot be mixed from several leaf types.

#### `mega_canopy.canopy_height` {#mega_canopy-canopy_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How many layers the cone has, drawn per tree.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. A drawn value of 0 places nothing. This is the shape's only random draw.

#### `mega_canopy.base_radius` {#mega_canopy-base_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 2 · range [0, −]</p>

**The half-width of the narrowest layer, at the very top.**

Every layer below widens by one from here, so this sets the whole cone's width, not just the tip's.

#### `mega_canopy.core_width` {#mega_canopy-core_width}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The width of the trunk this crown is built around. Must match it.**

Not a free setting: the feature is refused when it disagrees with the trunk's own width. At a branch tip the trunk is always one block wide, so a crown grown there needs 1.

#### `mega_canopy.simplify_canopy` {#mega_canopy-simplify_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · boolean · absent: false</p>

**Uses a strict circle for each layer instead of a relaxed one.**

With it off -- the default -- the corners of each layer are allowed through and the crown is fuller. With it on, every cell must fall inside the circle, which visibly shrinks each layer.

::::

:::: details `mega_pine_canopy` — 6 keys

#### `mega_pine_canopy` {#mega_pine_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**A tall conical crown for a wide trunk, widening in steps rather than one cell per layer.**

The same cone idea as mega_canopy but with the rate of widening under its own control, which is what makes it read as a pine rather than a jungle crown.

#### `mega_pine_canopy.leaf_block` {#mega_pine_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block every layer of the cone is built from.**

One block for the whole cone, tiers included -- the widening is a change of shape, never a change of block.

#### `mega_pine_canopy.canopy_height` {#mega_pine_canopy-canopy_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How many layers the cone has, drawn per tree.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. This is the shape's only random draw.

#### `mega_pine_canopy.base_radius` {#mega_pine_canopy-base_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 2 · range [0, −]</p>

**The half-width of the topmost layer.**

Every layer below is this plus whatever radius_step_modifier has added by then.

#### `mega_pine_canopy.radius_step_modifier` {#mega_pine_canopy-radius_step_modifier}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · number · absent: 3.5</p>

**How fast the cone widens going down. Larger means a wider, blunter cone.**

It scales the distance below the top before that distance is rounded down to whole cells, so a value below 1 makes several layers share a width and gives the crown visible tiers rather than a smooth flare.

#### `mega_pine_canopy.core_width` {#mega_pine_canopy-core_width}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The width of the trunk this crown is built around. Must match it.**

The feature is refused when it disagrees with the trunk's own width.

::::

:::: details `pine_canopy` — 4 keys

#### `pine_canopy` {#pine_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The narrow conical pine crown: diamond rings that shrink going up.**

One random draw jitters how far up the widest part sits, so two pines with identical settings still differ.

#### `pine_canopy.leaf_block` {#pine_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block every ring of the cone is built from.**

One block for the whole crown; this shape takes no second block, so the rings differ from each other only in width.

#### `pine_canopy.canopy_height` {#pine_canopy-canopy_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How tall the cone is, drawn per tree.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. It also sets the size of the second draw that jitters the cone vertically, so a taller cone is also a more variable one.

#### `pine_canopy.base_radius` {#pine_canopy-base_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The half-width the cone is allowed to reach at its widest.**

Where along the cone that width lands is what the jitter draw decides.

::::

:::: details `poplar_canopy` — 9 keys

#### `poplar_canopy` {#poplar_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · game build 1.26.50.24 -- whether the schema gates this key on format_version was NOT established, so it is offered at every version rather than hidden below one</p>

**A tall rounded crown of stacked diamonds with a cross of logs buried inside it.**

One coin flip per tree bulges a diagonal pair of quadrants outward by a cell, which is what gives a poplar its slightly lopsided silhouette. The top two layers have their outermost row and column trimmed so the crown rounds off instead of ending in a slab.

#### `poplar_canopy.leaf_block` {#poplar_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block the diamond layers are built from.**

The buried cross is branch_block instead; everything else is this.

#### `poplar_canopy.branch_block` {#poplar_canopy-branch_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The log used for the cross buried inside the crown.**

Placed four cells below the crown's top layer, reaching out along both horizontal axes with each arm's log turned to follow it. On a small crown the cross has no room and this block is never placed at all.

#### `poplar_canopy.radius` {#poplar_canopy-radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · groupList</p>

**The crown widths to choose between, with weights.**

One entry is picked per tree in proportion to its weight, and the crown it builds is one cell narrower than the entry says -- a value of 3 gives half-width-2 layers. Below a value of 5 the buried cross disappears entirely.

#### `poplar_canopy.radius.value` {#poplar_canopy-radius-value}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**One candidate width. The crown built is one cell narrower than this.**

That offset by one is easy to lose: writing 5 here is what a crown of half-width 4 needs.

#### `poplar_canopy.radius.weight` {#poplar_canopy-radius-weight}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 1</p>

**How often this width is picked, relative to the other entries.**

Weights are relative, not percentages, so doubling every entry changes nothing.

#### `poplar_canopy.height` {#poplar_canopy-height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How tall the crown is, drawn per tree.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. Unlike most ranges in this feature it includes its maximum.

#### `poplar_canopy.side_hole_chance` {#poplar_canopy-side_hole_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · number · absent: 0 -- no cell is pitted, though the roll is still spent on every cell</p>

**Chance to pull any one surface cell in by a block, pitting the crown.**

Mind the default, which is 0: no cell is ever pitted, and the crown comes out smooth. Worth knowing either way is that the roll happens for every candidate cell whether or not this key is written, so raising it changes the crown's look without changing how many random numbers the tree spends.

#### `poplar_canopy.trunk_width` {#poplar_canopy-trunk_width}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · integer · absent: 1</p>

**Checked against the trunk's own width. It does not change the crown's shape.**

Every trunk that can carry a poplar crown hands it a one-block footprint, so the geometry is the same whatever is written here. Listed so that finding it in an existing file is not mistaken for a width setting that stopped working.

::::

:::: details `roofed_canopy` — 6 keys

#### `roofed_canopy` {#roofed_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The thick flat-topped crown of a dark forest: a solid floor, a hipped roof above it, and a peak.**

The floor below the anchor is a full solid square; the roof at the top is that same square with its corners chamfered off. One coin flip decides whether a single cell is placed on top as a peak, and that flip is spent on every tree whatever the other settings say.

#### `roofed_canopy.leaf_block` {#roofed_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block the floor, the filling and the roof are all built from.**

One block for all three parts -- there is no way to give the roof a different block from the floor on this shape.

#### `roofed_canopy.canopy_height` {#roofed_canopy-canopy_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**How far above the anchor the roof sits, and how many layers of leaves fill the gap.**

A height of 0 is legal and is not the same as placing nothing: the floor, the roof and the coin-flipped peak are all still placed, and only the filling between them is skipped.

#### `roofed_canopy.core_width` {#roofed_canopy-core_width}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**The width of the trunk this crown is built around. Must match it.**

The feature is refused when it disagrees with the trunk's own width.

#### `roofed_canopy.outer_radius` {#roofed_canopy-outer_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · absent: the game treats this key as optional, but what it falls back to has not been established, so a value is asked for here rather than guessed · range [-1, −]</p>

**The half-width of the floor and the roof.**

A value of -1 is legal and means exactly one thing: skip the floor and the roof entirely. The coin flip and its peak still happen. Anything below -1 is refused.

#### `roofed_canopy.inner_radius` {#roofed_canopy-inner_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · absent: the game treats this key as optional, but what it falls back to has not been established, so a value is asked for here rather than guessed · range [0, −]</p>

**The half-width of the solid block of leaves stacked between the floor and the roof.**

Filled, not hollow, with its four corners cut. Set it below the outer radius and the floor and roof overhang it like a brim; set it to 0 and the two slabs are joined by a single column.

::::

:::: details `spruce_canopy` — 5 keys

#### `spruce_canopy` {#spruce_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**The layered spruce crown: bands that grow wide, snap back to nothing and grow again.**

That grow-and-reset is the whole shape -- it is what gives a spruce its alternating full and skinny bands instead of the single smooth taper every other conical shape here has.

#### `spruce_canopy.leaf_block` {#spruce_canopy-leaf_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block every band of the crown is built from.**

One block for the whole crown; the alternating bands are a change of width, not of block, so they read as one material throughout.

#### `spruce_canopy.lower_offset` {#spruce_canopy-lower_offset}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far below the trunk top the crown reaches, drawn per tree.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. Together with the upper offset it sets how many bands there is room for.

#### `spruce_canopy.upper_offset` {#spruce_canopy-upper_offset}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range · absent: the game treats this key as optional, but what it falls back to has not been established, so a value is asked for here rather than guessed</p>

**How far above the trunk top the crown starts, drawn per tree.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. The crown is built downward from here.

#### `spruce_canopy.max_radius` {#spruce_canopy-max_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**The widest a band may get before it snaps back, drawn per tree.**

It is doing two jobs at once: the drawn value caps each band, and the SPAN between the two ends of the range decides how wide the first band is allowed to get before the first reset. So widening the range changes the banding pattern, not just the maximum width.

::::

:::: details `random_spread_canopy` — 5 keys

#### `random_spread_canopy` {#random_spread_canopy}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group</p>

**Leaves scattered at random around the trunk rather than arranged in layers.**

Like mangrove_canopy it works from every log the trunk placed, not just the top one. Paired with the plain trunk or the cherry trunk it is handed an empty list, places nothing and draws nothing, leaving a bare pole -- pair it with the acacia, mega or mangrove trunk instead.

#### `random_spread_canopy.canopy_height` {#random_spread_canopy-canopy_height}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far up and down a scattered leaf may land, drawn once for the whole crown.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. Drawn once per tree and then reused for every attempt.

#### `random_spread_canopy.canopy_radius` {#random_spread_canopy-canopy_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far sideways a scattered leaf may land, drawn once for the whole crown.**

A range, so it wants range_min and range_max. Drawn once per tree, like the height.

#### `random_spread_canopy.leaf_placement_attempts` {#random_spread_canopy-leaf_placement_attempts}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer · range [0, −]</p>

**How many leaves are attempted around each trunk log.**

Multiplied by the number of logs the trunk collected, so a tall trunk makes a much denser crown for the same number here. An attempt that lands somewhere it may not build is lost rather than retried.

#### `random_spread_canopy.leaf_blocks` {#random_spread_canopy-leaf_blocks}

<p class="fl-facts">required · weightedBlockList</p>

**The blocks the scattered leaves are picked from, with weights.**

Write each entry as a two-element pair: the block first, then its weight. The list may not be empty. A fresh pick is made for every leaf, so a mixed list gives one tree a mixed crown.

::::

#### `base_block` {#base_block}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · blockList · a single descriptor is accepted as a one-element list</p>

**The block laid under the trunk once the tree is built.**

A finishing touch applied after the trunk and canopy are in place, so it overwrites whatever the ground turned out to be rather than deciding where the tree may grow -- that is may_grow_on.

A single descriptor or a list; both are accepted.

#### `may_grow_on` {#may_grow_on}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · blockList</p>

**Blocks the tree is willing to root on.**

Tested at the ground under the trunk. If the ground does not pass, the first entry in this list is placed there to make it pass -- so this list also decides what a tree stands on when it lands somewhere unsuitable.

#### `may_grow_through` {#may_grow_through}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · blockList</p>

**Blocks the trunk may push through on its way up.**

Applies BELOW the tree's own origin. At and above the origin the trunk is governed by may_replace instead, which is the distinction that catches people out when a trunk stops short in undergrowth.

#### `may_replace` {#may_replace}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · blockList</p>

**Blocks the tree may overwrite at and above its origin.**

Below the origin it is may_grow_through that decides instead.

:::: details `base_cluster` — 4 keys

#### `base_cluster` {#base_cluster}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: no ground patch is laid</p>

**A patch of ground laid under a wide trunk.**

Only the wide-trunk shape reads it; on any other trunk it is accepted and does nothing. The whole object is optional, but all three of its keys are required once it is there -- half of it is refused, not defaulted.

#### `base_cluster.may_replace` {#base_cluster-may_replace}

<p class="fl-facts">required · blockList</p>

**The blocks a patch may overwrite.**

An empty list is not the same as leaving the key out: with nothing listed, no patch is ever laid.

#### `base_cluster.num_clusters` {#base_cluster-num_clusters}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**How many patches to lay.**

A whole number, not a range -- unlike most sizes on this type. Writing `{range_min, range_max}` here is refused rather than read as a range. Nothing enforces a minimum: 0 or less loads clean and lays no patch at all.

#### `base_cluster.cluster_radius` {#base_cluster-cluster_radius}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**How far a patch reaches from its own centre.**

A whole number, not a range, for the same reason as the count beside it. Nothing enforces a minimum here either: at 0 or less every patch comes out empty, so no ground is replaced.

::::

:::: details `mangrove_roots` — 12 keys

#### `mangrove_roots` {#mangrove_roots}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: the tree stands on no roots</p>

**The stilt roots a mangrove stands on.**

Leaving it out means no roots at all, not roots of some default shape.

#### `mangrove_roots.max_root_width` {#mangrove_roots-max_root_width}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**How far the roots may spread from the trunk.**

Nothing enforces a minimum: 0 or less loads clean and behaves the same either way -- the roots never step sideways, they only drop straight down under the trunk.

#### `mangrove_roots.max_root_length` {#mangrove_roots-max_root_length}

<p class="fl-facts">required · integer</p>

**How long one root may grow before it stops.**

Nothing enforces a minimum, but 0 or less is fatal rather than inert: the root pass fails on the first direction and the whole tree is abandoned -- no roots, no trunk, no canopy.

#### `mangrove_roots.y_offset` {#mangrove_roots-y_offset}

<p class="fl-facts">required · range</p>

**How far above or below the trunk base the roots start.**

Drawn once per tree, so two trees from the same settings can start their roots at different heights.

#### `mangrove_roots.root_block` {#mangrove_roots-root_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block a root is built from in open air.**

#### `mangrove_roots.muddy_root_block` {#mangrove_roots-muddy_root_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block a root is built from where it passes through mud.**

#### `mangrove_roots.mud_block` {#mangrove_roots-mud_block}

<p class="fl-facts">required · block</p>

**The block laid as mud around the roots.**

#### `mangrove_roots.roots_may_grow_through` {#mangrove_roots-roots_may_grow_through}

<p class="fl-facts">required · blockList</p>

**The blocks a root may pass through.**

A root that meets a block not listed here stops there; the rest of the roots carry on.

#### `mangrove_roots.above_root` {#mangrove_roots-above_root}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · group · absent: nothing is placed on top of a root</p>

**An optional block placed on top of a finished root.**

Both of its keys are optional; with neither set, nothing is placed.

#### `mangrove_roots.above_root.above_root_chance` {#mangrove_roots-above_root-above_root_chance}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · chance · absent: never placed</p>

**How often a finished root gets a block on top of it.**

#### `mangrove_roots.above_root.above_root_block` {#mangrove_roots-above_root-above_root_block}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · block</p>

**The block placed on top of a root.**

#### `mangrove_roots.root_decoration` {#mangrove_roots-root_decoration}

<p class="fl-facts">optional · json · absent: roots are left undecorated</p>

**A decoration attached to the finished roots.**

The same shape a trunk decoration takes. Its own keys are not described at this path yet, so it is edited as JSON.
